findings.evidence: AccessMethods.lean:169-172 vs 178-181; the two field lists differ only by the substitution of `q`.
findings.fix: Introduce one definition, e.g. `invariantsOfTransfer (g : Bilin V) (p k q : V) : ReconstructedInvariants` with those three fields (or reuse `DisKinematics.xBj/Q2/yInel`), define `electronMethod g k p kPrime := invariantsOfTransfer g p k (k - kPrime)` and `hadronicMethod g k p pX := invariantsOfTransfer g p k (pX - p)` (both `rfl`), and state `x = Q2 / (2 * g p q)` and `x = Q2 / (2 * g p k * y)` once there. Each method keeps exactly the arguments it measures, as roadmap 1.2 requires.
findings.issue: `electronMethod g k p kPrime` (169-172) and `hadronicMethod g k p pX` (178-181) have identical bodies with `q := k - kPrime` resp. `q := pX - p`: `x = -g q q / (2 * g p q)`, `Q2 = -g q q`, `y = g p q / g p k`. The general result (the invariants of a transfer `q`) is never stated, so every relation among `x`, `Q2`, `y` has to be reproved per method; the PR already shows this gap — `electronMethod_disKinematics` (line 228) exists but has no hadronic analogue even though the hadronic method is the same map.

findings.evidence: `grep -r 'ElectronMethodData\|q2Electron\|xBjElectron\|yElectron'` over `code/` matches only `Kinematics/AccessMethods.lean` and `Kinematics/Radiative.lean` (the latter only via the covariant `electronMethod`).
findings.fix: Either prove the reduction (`electronMethod_lab_formula`: specialise `electronMethod` in a concrete collider frame and recover `q2Electron`, `yElectron`, `xBjElectron`), or delete `ElectronMethodData` and its lemmas, which have no in-repository use and are superseded by the covariant definition.
findings.issue: `ElectronMethodData` with `q2Electron`/`yElectron`/`xBjElectron` is the collider-frame special case of the new covariant `electronMethod`, in the same module, with no proved reduction (the docstrings at 56-60 and 163-167 say so) and no user anywhere in the repo. Roadmap convention 2 and §1.2 (`electronMethod_lab_formula`) put the lab formulae at the level of lemmas about the covariant definition; as it stands the PR leaves two unrelated electron methods and nothing forces them to agree. Note the PR did the right thing for Sigma: `sigmaMethod` is built on `SigmaMethodData.ySigma`.

findings.evidence: Radiative.lean:158-162 `neg_apply_smul_sub` is proved by `ring` with no hypotheses and its docstring says it "holds without any mass-shell condition on `u` or `v`"; Radiative.lean:409-411 then discards the `z * g e.k e.k` term via `hk`.
findings.fix: State the hypothesis-free form `(e.trueInvariants g .initialState).Q2 = z * (electronMethod g e.k e.p e.kPrime).Q2 + (1 - z) * (z * g e.k e.k - g e.kPrime e.kPrime)` and derive the current `hk = 0` version as a one-line corollary for the downstream users (`trueInvariants_Q2_lt_...`, `electronMethod_x_of_...`, `sigmaMethod_x_eq_...`), which do need `hk`.
findings.issue: `trueInvariants_Q2_of_collinear_initialState` assumes `hk : g e.k e.k = 0`, but the identity holds with no mass-shell hypothesis at all: applying the module's own `neg_apply_smul_sub` with `u = k`, `v = k'` to `pX - p = z • k - k'` gives `Q² = z * Q²_e + (1 - z) * (z * g k k - g k' k')`. This contradicts roadmap convention 9 ("The lepton mass is kept nonzero throughout") and the module docstring's own stated style (lines 61-63: the other lepton's mass "appears as an explicit remainder"), which the FSR counterpart at line 507 follows by keeping `g e.k e.k` as a remainder.

summary: The covariant methods and the collinear shift theorems sit at a reasonable level, but `electronMethod` and `hadronicMethod` are the same function duplicated, the new covariant electron method leaves the pre-existing frame-specific `ElectronMethodData` as an unreconciled second electron method, and the ISR virtuality theorem assumes a masslessness it does not need.
